title: Audit trace TTL and linking heuristics - notes v0.2
content:
Purpose:

This is a working doc to capture heuristic proposals for: (1) trace-level TTL semantics for audit events and linked evidence, (2) lightweight linking conventions for cross-service evidence (e.g. presigned blobs, SIEM references, encrypted evidence handles), and (3) compatibility constraints across schema v1→v3. Goal is to create a small set of pragmatic rules that the exporter, SIEM adapter, and Dedicated/Private control planes can implement consistently.

Summary (short):
- Problem: audit frames today have inconsistent "trace" lifetimes, and evidence pointers often leak transient handles or require heavyweight rehydration. This causes difficulties for SIEM ingestion, retention policy enforcement, and forensics workflows.
- Proposal: attach explicit trace_ttl_seconds to top-level audit frames, require evidence_refs to carry a canonical evidence_type and expiry, and add a lightweight "link_fingerprint" for idempotent stitching across systems.

Compatibility notes (v1→v3):
- v1: event-centric, only event_id + timestamp; no canonical trace id; evidence stored in ad-hoc evidence blob entries.
- v2: added trace_id and evidence_refs, but TTL semantics were underspecified and implementations diverged.
- v3 (target): explicit schema fields below, deterministic linking rules, and canonical export transformations for SIEM.

Core schema suggestions (top-level fields to standardize):
- event_id: string (UUID)
- event_type: string (namespace.action e.g. auth.login.succeeded)
- event_version: string (semver-lite, e.g. "v1", "v2")
- schema_version: string for audit schema (e.g. "audit-svc/3")
- timestamp: ISO-8601
- actor: { id, type, principal_source }  <-- free-form but encouraged fields (note: examples below)
- resource: free-form map (resource_type, resource_id)
- action: short verb
- trace_id: string (GUID)  -- used for grouping related events; MUST be propagated by callers when an operation spans services
- trace_ttl_seconds: integer (optional) -- time after which the trace and its evidence are considered stale for export and long-term retention policies (see heuristics)
- evidence_refs: list of evidence entries where each entry is a map with the following canonical string fields: evidence_id, evidence_type, location_hint (e.g. s3://, presigned-url), expiry_iso, link_fingerprint, origin_service
- link_fingerprint: string -- deterministic fingerprint of (evidence_type + evidence_id + origin_service) to dedupe in SIEM/export pipelines

Note: Because the Drive doc must be a flat payload here, we show example payloads below as JSON text blobs. Implementations will still send JSON objects in the wire format.

Example minimal event (text blob):
{
  "event_id": "6f9a7b10-9c3f-4a2a-bd2f-3b8b7fae2c01",
  "event_type": "auth.login.succeeded",
  "event_version": "v1",
  "schema_version": "audit-svc/3",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-02T18:12:34Z",
  "actor": "user:alice@redwood.ai",
  "resource": "session:78ef",
  "action": "create",
  "trace_id": "t-4c5d6e7f-0001",
  "trace_ttl_seconds": 2592000,  
  "evidence_refs": [
    {
      "evidence_id": "e-12345",
      "evidence_type": "session-recording",
      "location_hint": "s3://redwood-audit/session-e-12345.mp4",
      "expiry_iso": "2026-06-30T00:00:00Z",
      "link_fingerprint": "sha256:abcd...",
      "origin_service": "session-recorder"
    }
  ]
}

Heuristics for trace_ttl_seconds:
- Default TTL: 30 days (2592000 sec) for user-facing traces.
- Short TTL (7 days) for ephemeral system-internal traces (internal health probes, ephemeral autoscaling signals).
- Long TTL (365 days) only when evidence is regulatory/legal (flagged in evidence_type) or requested by legal holds (override header).
- If any evidence_refs have expiry_iso earlier than trace_ttl_seconds, the exporter MUST honor the earliest expiry when calculating SIEM-level retention tags.

Linking and idempotency rules:
- Every evidence_ref MUST include link_fingerprint (deterministic hash). SIEM adapters should dedupe on trace_id + link_fingerprint + evidence_type.
- When an evidence handle is rotated (new presigned URL), the evidence_id remains the canonical id; location_hint can change. link_fingerprint should be computed from evidence_id + origin_service to remain stable.
- If multiple events include the same evidence_id and trace_id, they SHOULD be folded by downstream exporters rather than duplicated.

SIEM export adapter notes (practical):
- Exporter responsibility: convert evidence_refs into SIEM-friendly metadata: evidence_id, evidence_type, evidence_availability (boolean), evidence_link_sha256, evidence_expiry. Avoid sending presigned-URLs to external SIEMs—send a stable evidence_id and an optional short-lived access token exchange endpoint (internal).
- Enrichments: add fields: siem_grouping_key = join(trace_id, schema_version), siem_retention_tag = derive(retention policy from trace_ttl_seconds and evidence types).

Backward/forward compatibility approach:
- Maintain event_version and schema_version fields on every event. Consumers should use schema_version primarily. event_version can be used for finer-grained decoding.
- For rolling deploys, follow these rules: v2->v3 compatibility mode: when `schema_version` is missing assume v2 decoding rules and synthesize trace_ttl_seconds = 30d; add a warning flag in the exported message.

Edge cases and unresolved questions:
- Q1: Who owns the canonical evidence lifecycle? (origin_service vs audit-store). Suggestion: origin_service owns the blob lifecycle; audit-store keeps evidence metadata and a retention tag.
- Q2: Should trace_ttl_seconds be mutable per trace? (yes, allow updates but require change events to be emitted if decreased).
- Q3: How to handle cross-tenant evidence linking in Dedicated/Private? We may need namespacing in link_fingerprint (tenant_id + evidence_id) to prevent collisions.
- Q4: Performance: computing link_fingerprint on very high event rates — suggest an optional sampling mode where link_fingerprint is only attached for evidence_refs with type in a configured allowlist.

Migration notes and rollout plan (high level):
- Step 0: Publish heuristic doc and gather feedback (this draft).
- Step 1: Library changes — audit-sdk adds trace_ttl_seconds and evidence_ref validation (2 weeks).
- Step 2: Exporter changes — SIEM adapter implements dedupe on link_fingerprint and retention tagging (2 weeks).
- Step 3: Canary: roll to one region and one Dedicated customer for 2 weeks, monitor duplicate counts and retention mismatches.
- Step 4: Gradual global rollout with opt-in for legal-hold overrides.

Acceptance criteria for v3 rollout:
- No more than 1% increase in duplicate evidence entries in SIEM exports post-rollout.
- All evidence_refs originating in our primary services include link_fingerprint >= 95% of events.
- Trace grouping by trace_id reduces forensic assembly time in the internal triage tool by >= 30% in canary tests.

Appendix: quick checklist for implementers
- [ ] SDK: add trace_id propagation helper and default trace_ttl_seconds value.
- [ ] Services: always include evidence_type and origin_service on evidence_refs.
- [ ] Exporters: never send raw presigned URLs to external SIEM; send stable evidence_id + exchange endpoint instead.
- [ ] Compliance: add mapping from evidence_type to retention policy in compliance catalog.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we aim to reduce friction for SIEM vendors while preserving forensic fidelity. Please annotate sections that will cause engineering or compliance churn.
- Related tickets: jira:SEC-4572 (evidence-linking), jira:SEC-4630 (siem-dedupe), github:infra/audit-exporter#2345 (exporter dedupe implementation).

-- Aisha (draft, 2026-06-05)
